metadata.title: Common Shade Module F — Thailand
metadata.method: Targeted Thai/English primary-source review, selected legal/report sections and original research abstracts; not exhaustive systematic review.
metadata.city_selection: Eight documented heat-concern cities selected using TMD station records, Bangkok evidence and climate/context variety. National most-exposed ranking not verified; no rank assigned.
metadata.no_endorsement: No organisation ranked; listing implies no partnership or endorsement.
metadata.taxonomy_note: Functional website mapping only; university health research is not legal health authority. Proposed roles and loop links are interpretation.
metadata.cost_rule: Missing installed/operating/upkeep costs and FX are null, not zero; no universal price or unsupported FX conversion.
retrieval_limits: DEDE BEC pages/PDF returned502; exact legal scope numerical thresholds excluded.
World Bank full Bangkok PDF exceeded retrieval size; official study summary used.
WIEGO PDF text garbled; methods page visually checked, other claims bounded to accessible publisher summary.
WHO national HHAP table and narrative disagree in status; final adoption instrument not verified.
BMA Heat Index source has imprecise exact52°C boundary; no executable trigger encoded.

country.name: Thailand

climate.text: Monsoonal climate: hot-humid exposure especially Bangkok/southern lowlands, with seasonally drier intense heat inland; evaluate humidity by season and time rather than treating Thailand as one cooling climate.
climate.result_basis: Context synthesis; local cooling suitability is a researcher assessment.

night_heat.text: 1970–2024 analysis finds growing independent hot-night and compound hot-event exposure; station-district coverage does not establish every city’s bedroom conditions.

temperature_record.sample: TMD station aggregate; exact station count not reported in reviewed summary
temperature_record.result_basis: Observed national aggregate, not city health exposure

plans.text: WHO2026 profile lists Health National Adaptation Plan Phase1(2021–2030) as approved and under revision. It marks a heat-health plan present for2025 while its note describes further national plan development as forthcoming. Final standalone HHAP text, adoption date and legal instrument not verified.

Bangkok2026 urban-heat response is reported, but February BMA account describes submitting a draft for approval; October UNDP strategy references the urban-heat plan. Signed adoption instrument and final annexes not retrieved.

plans.text: September2026 AIT/Vital Strategies account describes development of an integrated evidence-based Bangkok HHAP and roadmap. This is distinct from seasonal cooling-centre response.
ADB2026 suggests a national HAP roadmap; an external recommended roadmap is not an adopted government obligation.

warning_systems.text: WHO documents DOH/TMD heat-health information integration, with a shift to Heat Index in2025, official dashboards and risk communication. Offline receipt and uniform local activation/finance arrangements not verified.
BMA publishes colour-coded Heat Index guidance. Heat Index, WBGT, dry-bulb air temperature and satellite land-surface temperature cannot safely be interchanged.

legal_basis.text: Ministerial Regulation on occupational heat/light/noise B.E.2559(2016), under the Occupational Safety, Health and Environment Act B.E.2554(2011), published17October2016. Current labour authority provides text and measurement notifications; full later-amendment audit not completed.

sources.url: https://osh.labour.go.th/ร้อน-แสง-เสียง-2559/

occupational_heat_rules.measurement: Law defines average WBGT during the hottest two hours of normal work, with workload classes; obtain qualified assessment for the specific task.
occupational_heat_rules.legal_controls: Warning signs, engineering correction and documentation; workload controls where engineering cannot meet standard.
occupational_heat_rules.caveat: These are statutory WBGT limits, not a universal ambient-temperature stop-work rule, proof of universal physiological safety or automatic entitlement for all self-employed workers. Paid rest and enforcement would be worth verifying locally.

research.text: Thai observational construction/foundry study found heat strain among some workers even under compliant conditions; do not interpret compliance as a guarantee.

cooling_and_building_policy.text: ADB discusses heat-policy options and passive/active cooling. Detailed BEC scope and current amendments require direct DEDE/legal verification because DEDE pages returned502; no numerical building-coverage threshold presented as verified here.
EGAT Label No.5 provides a current route to compare certified equipment; updated stars introduced2024. Check the exact model and operating assumptions.

UNEP treaty record lists Thailand Kigali ratification3April2024 and HFC licensing; DIW national ozone unit is the counterpart. A treaty commitment does not verify a particular appliance refrigerant or servicing practice.
